title: Banding column contract declares produced output even when the factor has no rules (runtime skips it)
description: _banding_columns reports a factor's outputColumn as a produced column whenever both 'column' and 'outputColumn' are non-empty: `produced = {f["outputColumn"] for f in factors if f.get("outputColumn")}`. But the runtime _apply_banding_factors skips any factor whose rules are empty: `if not col or not out or not rules: continue`. So a banding factor with column+outputColumn set but an empty/absent `rules` list is declared as produced by the contract yet is never created at runtime. The projection demand-propagation subtracts produced columns from upstream demand (projection.py:2321 `base_contribution = (my_needed - produced) | referenced`), so if a downstream node demands that outputColumn, the demand is removed at the banding node (contract claims ownership) but no column is materialised -> downstream select/reference fails with column-not-found in projected/bounded profiles. The contract must apply the same `rules` guard as the executor.
evidence: _banding_columns (l.762) has no rules check; _apply_banding_factors (_rating.py l.244) skips factors with empty rules; projection.py l.2321 subtracts `produced` from upstream demand for concrete contracts (BANDING is concrete, registered via columns=_banding_columns at l.767).
